para.text: In this chapter, the following terms have the meanings indicated.
Terms Defined.
“Care coordinator” means an employee of the justice-involved correctional facility provider that meets the certification and training requirements delineated in Regulation .03 of this chapter.
“Department” has the meaning stated in COMAR 10.09.36.01.
“Entity” means a:
State or locally operated correctional agency;
Correctional facility operated by local jurisdictions or the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; or
Secure residential facility operated by the Maryland Department of Juveniles Services.
“Inmate of a Public Institution” has the meaning stated in COMAR 10.09.24.02.
“Justice-involved correctional facility provider” means an entity that:
Was approved by the Department to coordinate, oversee, and monitor justice-involved case management services rendered by qualified care coordinators;
Employs care coordinators; and
Meets the qualifications set forth in Regulation .04 of this chapter.
“Medical Assistance Program” has the meaning stated in COMAR 10.09.36.01.
Justice-Involved Case Management.
“Justice-involved case management” means case management services which will assist eligible participants to gain access to needed medical, social, educational, and other services.

“Justice-involved case management” includes activities involved in developing, revising, implementing, and monitoring the person-centered care plan, as described in Regulation .05 of this chapter, and performed by a care coordinator through an approved justice-involved correctional facility provider.
“Participant” means an individual who is certified as eligible for and is receiving Medical Assistance benefits.
“Person-centered care plan” means a plan that:
Addresses physical, behavioral health, and health related social needs;
Considers additional services and supports, either pre-release or post-release;
Engages the participant at the center of decision making; and
May include recommendations based on assessments conducted by other staff or community providers serving the participant.
“Program” has the meaning stated in COMAR 10.09.36.01.
“Serious mental illness” has the meaning stated in COMAR 10.21.17.02.
“Substance use disorder” has the meaning stated in COMAR 10.09.06.02.
Eligibility with a Qualified Diagnosis. A participant with a qualifying diagnosis as described in §B of this regulation is eligible for justice-involved case management services if the individual:
Is 18 years or older;
Is an inmate of a public institution due to having received a sentence of incarceration; and
Will be released from a public institution within 90 days.
Qualified Diagnoses. A qualifying diagnosis includes diagnosis of:
A substance use disorder;
A serious mental illness; or
Both a substance use disorder and a serious mental illness.
Eligibility without a Qualified Diagnosis.

A participant without a qualifying diagnosis as described in §B of this regulation is eligible for justice-involved case management services if the individual meets one of the criteria in both §C(2) and (3) of this regulation.
Age Criteria. The individual shall meet one of the following age criteria:
Be younger than 21 years old; or
Be a former foster care child between the ages of 18 and 26.
Inmate Criteria. After having been found by a court to have committed a criminal or delinquent offense, the individual shall meet one of the following inmate criteria:
Be an inmate of a public institution who will be released from a public institution within 30 days; or
Was an inmate of a public institution who has been released from a public institution in the past 30 days.
Participant Consent. A participant shall consent to receive justice-involved case management services.
A participant may not receive justice-involved case management services if they are receiving comparable services under §1915(b), 1915(c), or 1915(g) of 42 U.S.C 1396n.

Care coordinators shall have completed all certification and training requirements set by the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services or the Department of Juvenile Services for care coordinators.

Care coordinators shall maintain the applicable certification from the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services or the Department of Juvenile Services without lapse while employed by a justice-involved correctional facility provider.
General Program Requirements. A justice-involved correctional facility provider shall meet the general requirements for participation in the Program including:
Meeting all the conditions for participation set forth in COMAR 10.09.36; and
If delivering services via telehealth, comply with COMAR 10.09.49 and any applicable subregulatory guidance issued by the Department.
Justice-involved correctional facility providers shall:
Employ care coordinators who meet minimum educational and experience requirements established by the Department;
Ensure employed care coordinators are properly certified in accordance with Regulation .03 of this chapter;
Attest to compliance with the duties regarding provision of justice-involved case management, in the manner required by the Department;
Ensure that care coordinators have the capacity to meet with participants in-person or via telehealth;
Ensure care coordinators are aware of and receive training on the eligibility requirements and application procedures of applicable federal, State, and local government assistance programs; and

Maintain a current listing of medical, social, housing assistance, mental health, financial assistance, counseling, and other support services available to participants receiving justice-involved case management services.
Record Keeping Requirements.
Justice-involved correctional facility providers shall maintain the following records for each participant receiving services:
Verification of the participant's eligibility for services;
A consent form signed by the participant, or the participant’s parent or guardian, consenting to participate in justice-involved case management services;
A signed consent form authorizing the provider to disclose the participant's health care information for purposes of care coordination;
A complete person-centered care plan, updated as needed; and
Documentation of each justice-involved case management contact made with the participant including:
The date of the contact;
The topic of the contact
The person contacted;
The care coordinator making the contact; and
The modality of service and, if services were rendered in-person, the location of the contact.
Justice-involved correctional facility providers shall maintain records demonstrating compliance with §B of this regulation.
Justice-involved correctional facility providers shall make records available to the Department for inspection upon request.

Effective October 23, 2025, the Program covers justice-involved case management services when a participant receives all case management services described in §B of this regulation in a 30-day period.
Justice-involved Case Management Services. Justice-involved case management services include the following:
Comprehensive assessment and periodic reassessment of participant needs, to determine the need for any medical, educational, social, or other services;
Development and periodic revision of a person-centered care plan based on the information collected through the assessment;
Referral and related activities to help the participant obtain needed supportive and stabilizing services necessary to address needs and goals specified in the person-centered care plan; and
Monitoring and follow-up activities with the participant, family members, and service providers necessary to ensure that the person-centered care plan is effectively implemented.
The Program shall cover justice-involved case management services if:
The services are provided by a care coordinator;
The services are documented in the person-centered care plan; and
The care coordinator provides a minimum of three visits to the participant to provide justice-involved case management services, during the 30-day period.
Care coordinators shall:
Assist with the development or revision of the person-centered care plan by:
Incorporating results from any relevant assessments into the person-centered care plan;
Participating in the development or revision of a person-centered care plan for the participant;
Encouraging the participant’s participation in the development and periodic updating of the person-centered care plan; and
Linking the participant with any services needed on an emergency basis before the person-centered care plan or revision of the plan is finalized;
Assume responsibility for providing case management services to the participant;
Act as a point of contact for the participant’s case; and
Implement and monitor the participant’s person-centered care plan.
Justice-involved case management services shall be advisory in nature.
A restriction may not be placed by the justice-involved correctional facility provider upon eligible individuals’ option to receive justice-involved case management services.
Justice-involved case management services may not restrict or otherwise affect:
Eligibility for Title XIX benefits or other available benefits or programs; or
The freedom of a participant to select from all available services for which the individual is found to be eligible.
Justice-involved case management services may not be rendered in connection with the implementation of §1915(b) or 1915(c) of 42 U.S.C 1396n.

Managed Care Organizations or the Behavioral Health Administrative Services Organization providing post-release justice-involved case management services may not be reimbursed through fee for service and shall instead be reimbursed in accordance with their individual contracts with the state.
A participant's justice-involved case management care coordinator may not be a provider of direct services for the participant.
Justice-involved case management services may not result in a delayed release from a public institution.
Providers shall bill the Program for services in accordance with COMAR 10.09.36.04.
Billing time limitations for claims submitted pursuant to this chapter are set forth in COMAR 10.09.36.06.
Effective October 23, 2025, the rate for justice-involved case management services is $561.05 per participant per 30-day period of service.

section.heading: Recovery and Reimbursement.
section.text: Recovery and reimbursement shall be as set forth in COMAR 10.09.36.07.

section.heading: Cause for Suspension or Removal and Imposition of Sanctions.
section.text: Cause for suspension or removal from the Program and imposition of sanctions shall be as set forth in COMAR 10.09.36.08.

section.heading: Filing Appeal.
section.text: Appeal procedures shall be as set forth in COMAR 10.09.36.09.

section.heading: Interpretive Regulation.
section.text: State regulations shall be interpreted as set forth in COMAR 10.09.36.10.
